issues.t: Front strut housing rusts and cracks (recall)
issues.sym: Rust holes or flaking metal around the front strut towers under the hood, clunks over bumps, one corner sitting lower, or steering that feels loose or wanders. In bad cases the strut can push up through the weakened housing.
issues.why: Road salt and water collect around the front strut housings and eat through the metal. Nissan recalled 1997-2003 QX4s sold or registered in salt-belt states to inspect and repair the housings.
issues.next: Have an Infiniti or Nissan dealer check the VIN for the open recall and inspect the strut towers. If the housing is cracked, do not drive the vehicle until it is repaired.

issues.t: Takata passenger airbag inflator can rupture (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning at all. You may have received a recall letter about the passenger front airbag.
issues.why: The Takata passenger airbag inflator can break down over time, especially in heat and humidity, and may burst when the airbag deploys, throwing metal pieces into the cabin.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open airbag recalls right away. Until it is fixed, keep passengers out of the front seat, and have the dealer replace the inflator free of charge.

issues.t: Fuel filler tube can rust and leak (recall)
issues.sym: A gasoline smell near the rear of the vehicle, wet spots or drips near the fuel filler, or fuel spitting back at the pump.
issues.why: The coating on the fuel filler tube was too thin in places, so salty water reached bare metal and rusted it through. A leaking filler tube is a fire risk.
issues.next: If you smell fuel, have it inspected promptly. Ask a dealer whether the filler tube recall has been done on your VIN; it is replaced free.

issues.t: Steering lock can engage from loose key cylinder pins (recall)
issues.sym: Keys or ignition that feel loose or odd, and in rare cases the steering wheel locking while the vehicle is moving.
issues.why: Pins in the ignition key cylinder connector could work loose, which could let the steering lock engage while driving.
issues.next: Ask a dealer to confirm the recall was done. If the key switch feels loose or the steering ever binds, stop driving and have it inspected.

issues.t: Rear hatch support brackets can bend and let the door drop (recall)
issues.sym: The rear liftgate will not stay up, sags or drops, especially on hot days.
issues.why: The brackets that hold the liftgate gas struts were too weak and could bend in high heat, so the open door could fall on someone.
issues.next: Do not stand under the open hatch if it sags. Have a dealer check the VIN and replace the brackets under the recall.

issues.t: Intake power valve screws loosen and fall into the engine
issues.sym: A check engine light, rough or unstable idle, loss of power, rattling from the top of the engine, or a sudden loud bang followed by a misfire or dead cylinder.
issues.why: Small screws that hold the butterfly valves inside the 3.5L engine's intake manifold can back out. If one is sucked into a cylinder, it can damage the valves, piston and cylinder wall. Owners of 2001-2004 VQ35 engines took Nissan to court over this.
issues.next: If you hear a rattle from the intake or the engine suddenly runs rough, stop and have it checked before driving further. Many owners have the screws secured with threadlocker as prevention while the intake is off.

issues.t: Stalling or no-start from a failing crank or cam sensor
issues.sym: The engine cuts out briefly while driving, stalls, cranks but will not start, or starts rough. A camshaft or crankshaft sensor code may be stored, though sometimes no light comes on.
issues.why: The crankshaft and camshaft position sensors on the 3.5L engine wear out. When one sends a weak or missing signal, the engine computer loses track of engine timing and cuts fuel and spark.
issues.next: Have the codes read. Replacing the faulty sensor, often with a genuine Nissan part, usually cures it. Because stalling in traffic is dangerous, do not put it off.

issues.t: Timing belt wear on the 3.3L engine
issues.sym: Ticking or slapping from the front of the engine, loss of power, or a sudden stall with the engine refusing to start.
issues.why: The 3.3L V6 uses a rubber timing belt that wears with age and miles. It is an interference engine, so if the belt breaks, valves and pistons can be damaged.
issues.next: If there is no record of a belt change in the last 100,000 miles or so, have it replaced now along with the water pump. If the belt has already snapped, have a compression test done before repairing.

issues.t: Water pump leak and overheating
issues.sym: Coolant drips at the front of the engine, a sweet smell, the temperature gauge climbing, or steam from under the hood.
issues.why: The water pump on the 3.3L engine is driven by the timing belt. Pumps that are not replaced at belt changes eventually leak or fail.
issues.next: Watch the temperature gauge and pull over if it climbs. Replace the water pump with the timing belt to avoid paying the labor twice.

issues.t: Valve cover gasket oil leaks
issues.sym: A burning oil smell, light smoke from the engine bay after driving, or oil seeping down the sides of the engine. Drips on the ground are less common.
issues.why: The rubber valve cover gaskets harden and crack after years of heat. Front and rear main seals and the oil pan gasket can also start to seep on high-mileage engines.
issues.next: Have the leak traced and fix it before oil soaks the exhaust or spark plug wells. Check the oil level regularly in the meantime.

issues.t: Fuel gauge bounces or reads wrong
issues.sym: The fuel gauge swings up and down, reads empty with fuel in the tank, or reads full for too long.
issues.why: The fuel level sending unit on the fuel pump wears where its contact sweeps the resistor strip, sending bad readings to the gauge. Nissan once extended coverage on this part.
issues.next: Track fuel by the trip odometer until it is fixed. The sending unit is replaced through the fuel pump access; some owners replace the pump at the same time.

issues.t: Knock sensor code P0325
issues.sym: Check engine light with code P0325. The engine usually runs normally, though some owners notice slightly weaker performance.
issues.why: The knock sensor and its wiring sit under the intake plenum at the back of the engine, where heat and age break them down.
issues.next: The parts are simple, but the repair takes time because the intake has to come off. Have the wiring checked first; if the sensor is replaced, do it together with other jobs under the intake.

issues.t: Rough idle and misfire codes from dirty injectors
issues.sym: Rough idle, hesitation when accelerating, and a check engine light with misfire codes P0300 to P0306.
issues.why: Deposits build up on the fuel injectors so they spray poorly. Infiniti issued a service bulletin with an injector cleaning procedure for this.
issues.next: Have the misfire codes read. An injector cleaning service often fixes it; if not, check plugs, wires and individual injectors.

issues.t: Erratic idle from a dirty throttle body
issues.sym: Idle speed that hunts up and down, stalls when coming to a stop, or a gas pedal that feels stiff at first.
issues.why: Carbon builds up around the throttle plate and idle passages, so the engine can't control idle air properly.
issues.next: Have the throttle body cleaned. It is a simple fix and often clears the idle problem.

issues.t: Check engine light from oxygen sensors
issues.sym: Check engine light, sometimes with worse fuel economy. Rear sensor codes such as P0138 or P0158 are common.
issues.why: Oxygen sensors wear out with age, and the rear (downstream) sensors are a known source of codes; Infiniti issued service bulletins for rear sensor codes on these years.
issues.next: Have the codes read and confirm there are no exhaust leaks. Replace the failed sensor with a direct-fit part.

issues.t: 4WD light flashing
issues.sym: The 4WD warning light flashes or comes on now and then, sometimes with no transfer case code stored.
issues.why: The All-Mode 4WD system watches tire sizes and wheel speeds. Mismatched tires, a weak sensor signal or wiring faults can set off the light; Infiniti issued a bulletin for intermittent 4WD lights.
issues.next: Check that all four tires are the same size and evenly worn. If the light stays, have the 4WD system scanned.

issues.t: Transfer case clunk or stuck in 4WD Low
issues.sym: A clunk from under the vehicle when shifting or starting off, or the transfer case refusing to come out of 4WD Low.
issues.why: Infiniti issued service bulletins for a clunk from the All-Mode transfer case and for the transfer case sticking in 4WD Low.
issues.next: Have a dealer or 4x4 shop check for the bulletin fix. Don't force the shift; use the procedure in the owner's manual.

issues.t: Transfer case oil leak
issues.sym: Oil drips under the middle of the vehicle, or a damp, oily transfer case.
issues.why: Seals on the transfer case can seep. Infiniti issued a service bulletin covering transfer case oil leaks on this generation.
issues.next: Have the leak confirmed and the fluid level checked. Running low on fluid can damage the transfer case.

issues.t: Front brake shudder when stopping
issues.sym: A shaking steering wheel or pulsing pedal when braking, often from highway speed, and sometimes brake noise.
issues.why: Front rotors develop uneven thickness. Infiniti issued service bulletins on brake judder, noise and pedal feel covering these years.
issues.next: Have the brakes checked. Replacing the front pads and rotors, or turning the rotors on the vehicle, usually fixes it.

issues.t: Grinding or humming from a worn wheel bearing
issues.sym: A hum or growl that gets louder with speed or changes when turning, play in the wheel, or an ABS light.
issues.why: Wheel bearings and hubs wear out on these heavy SUVs and are one of the most reported repairs in owner surveys.
issues.next: Have the bearing checked soon. A badly worn bearing can overheat and let the wheel wobble.

issues.t: Worn sway bar links and control arm bushings
issues.sym: Clunks or rattles over bumps, loose handling, or the SUV leaning more than usual in turns.
issues.why: Sway bar end links, control arm bushings and ball joints wear with age and are common repairs on QX4s.
issues.next: Have the front suspension inspected. Replace the worn parts and get an alignment afterward.

issues.t: Rear shake or wobble at highway speed
issues.sym: The rear of the SUV shakes, wobbles or feels unstable above about 50 mph, sometimes after new tires and an alignment didn't help.
issues.why: Owners report worn rear shocks, bushings and suspension links as common causes on high-mileage examples, though not every case has a clear fix.
issues.next: Have the rear shocks, suspension bushings, driveshaft and tires checked. Avoid highway driving if the shake is severe.

issues.t: Squeak or creak from the right rear shock
issues.sym: A squeak or creak from the back of the vehicle over bumps.
issues.why: Infiniti issued a service bulletin for a squeak at the right rear shock, sometimes caused by a stone caught around the mount.
issues.next: Have the rear shock mount area checked for debris and worn bushings.

issues.t: Cracked exhaust manifold or rattling heat shield
issues.sym: Ticking from the engine when cold, a louder exhaust, exhaust smell, a rattling heat shield, or a failed emissions test.
issues.why: Owners report cracked exhaust manifolds and loose heat shields on the 3.3L engine after many heat cycles.
issues.next: Have the exhaust inspected. Fix leaks near the engine promptly because fumes can reach the cabin.

issues.t: Won't start because the immobilizer doesn't recognize the key
issues.sym: The engine cranks but won't start, or won't start at all, and the security light blinks.
issues.why: The NATS immobilizer can fail to read the key chip. Infiniti issued service bulletins for no-start conditions tied to the immobilizer.
issues.next: Try the spare key. If it starts, the first key is the problem. Otherwise the dealer can diagnose the antenna ring or reprogram keys.

issues.t: Blower fan works only on top speed
issues.sym: The heater and A/C fan runs only on the highest setting, or not at all on lower speeds.
issues.why: The blower speed controller (fan control amplifier) fails. Infiniti issued a bulletin for blowers that only work on speed 4.
issues.next: Replacing the fan control amplifier under the dash usually fixes it.

issues.t: Roof console temperature display reads wrong
issues.sym: The outside temperature shown in the overhead console is clearly off.
issues.why: Infiniti issued a service bulletin for the console temperature display reading inaccurately.
issues.next: Ask a dealer about the bulletin fix; it is a comfort issue, not a safety one.

issues.t: Navigation screen freezes or reroutes
issues.sym: The navigation display freezes, reroutes on its own, or gives no voice guidance.
issues.why: Infiniti issued a service bulletin for these navigation faults on this generation.
issues.next: Ask a dealer whether a software or DVD update applies to your vehicle.

issues.t: Rearview mirror loose or falls off
issues.sym: The inside rearview mirror sags, moves or drops off the windshield.
issues.why: Infiniti issued a service bulletin for loose or detached rearview mirrors.
issues.next: Have the mirror reattached with the proper mounting adhesive.
